findings.reason: the section as written is unachievable, and a worker dispatched to it will either report a blocker or fabricate the before half, so §6 needs its base arm restated as something obtainable (a synthetic crew home, as §2–§4 use) or the before census dropped in favour of the per-run gates already landed.
findings.text: §6's done-when requires "A census of the live fleet after §2 to §5 have landed, beside the same census taken before", but §2–§5 are all `done` (landed 22 November, landed records in docs/evidence/fragments/a-claim-nobody-is-working-is-released/), no pre-landing census exists in any fragment, and the pre-landing fleet state cannot be reconstructed from the base revision because the pointers those sections released are already gone from the live directory — so the node cannot produce the half of its measure that shows the defect was there

findings.reason: after every section lands the census can pass while §7's case is still unwatched, so the plan's completion certificate covers four of its five claim kinds, and the fix is a declared wait of §6 on §7 plus a fifth row and a fifth census column.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` gives §6 waits on s2, s3, s4 and s5 only, and §6's census enumerates "promoted, measurement-only or landed-group run", so the plan's only whole-fleet measure never looks at the delivered-but-never-landed kind §7 delivers; §1's own map (lines 35–44) likewise states four kinds and stops at §5

findings.reason: the safety of the lapse is exactly the value of that interval, and with it unstated a worker can make the test green with an interval short enough to drop a live coordinator's claim, which is the failure §1's rule ("never released on an unknown reading") exists to prevent; the plan should state the interval or state the default constant and require the test to cross it.
findings.text: §7's deliverable says the claim lapses after "no coordinator action, landing attempt or review for a stated interval" and its done-when says only that the request "is admitted once the interval has passed", so the interval — the parameter the whole guard turns on — is left to the implementer and any value, including a trivially short one, satisfies the gate

findings.reason: the section has already landed as one node and its gate fails on either arm independently, so splitting it now would re-run landed work for no gain; recording it matters only if a future section repeats the shape.
findings.text: §5's deliverable conjoins two independent mechanisms: a resumed run reads as working only once its worker has begun a turn (with a failed-launch classification on the bound), and stopping any run ends every process the launch started and reports each pid

findings.reason: the line names files rather than symbols, formulas or step sequences, it is the authored template's declared field and is used uniformly by the five already-landed and reviewed sections, and removing it would also break the file-scoped dispatch the coordinator locks on — this is a template question, not a defect of this plan.
findings.text: every section carries a "Write paths" line naming the modules to extend (lines 51, 57, 63, 69, 74, 80), which is the reuse map the node brief is meant to compose, not a plan declaration
